Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra and security teams have reviewed the notes and we need to lock down a concrete maintenance cadence and rollback policy for our private deployment (VPC, on-prem connector) before we sign the final PO. Key asks from our side:

- A clear version-pinning policy (how long we keep a pinned version, forced updates, opt-in windows)
- Maintenance windows (preferred local times, outage expectations, canary strategy)
- Rollback / emergency unpin procedure and SLAs for mitigation
- Evidence for audit: runbooks, checklists, and a contact escalation ladder

Can you share a proposed cadence and sample runbook? Attaching the checklist the security team expects — please reference the section numbers in your response.

Appreciate it,
James

Hi James — thanks for the checklist and for summarizing the core asks. High level proposal below; I attached a compact maintenance cadence workbook for your team with mappings to your checklist (see tab "Orion mapping").

Summary (short):
- Version pinning: default pin for 90 days after GA in your private fleet; emergency security backports can be pushed with approval. Customers can request a longer pin (180d) via an enterprise flag in the console. (Checklist refs: 2.1, 2.3)
- Maintenance windows: recurring weekly 02:00–04:00 local window for low-risk patching; monthly >1h patch window scheduled with 72h notice for major/minor changes. Canary: 2 nodes (1% of fleet) for 48h before fleet-wide rollout. (Checklist refs: 3.2, 3.4)
- Rollback / emergency unpin: immediate unpin + automated traffic steering back to last-known-good variant. We recommend a two-tier rollback: fast-unpin (5–15 min propagate) and full-evacuation rollback (30–90 min) depending on KV cache invalidation. Runbook items: rollback criteria, health-signal gating, and rollback acceptance tests. (Checklist refs: 4.1, 4.4)
- Escalation ladder: on-call infra → private deployments PM → security lead → engineering director. We include audit logs for all pin/unpin and rollout actions. (Checklist refs: 5.1)

Proposed next steps:
1) Align on maintenance windows (we propose Tue/Wed 02:00–04:00 PT for initial staging runs).
2) We run a canary on your staging cluster next Tuesday; we’ll share telemetry and a short health report.
3) Sign off on the attached runbook (redwood-maintenance-cadence.xlsx).

Copying Karthik and Marissa to validate operational details and rollback timings.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in some operational specifics for the runbook and rollback SLAs. A few notes for your team and for James/Sasha to confirm:

- Pinning TTL and emergency patches: we can support 90d default pin + optional 180d via enterprise flag. Emergency security patches (CVSS >= 7.0) will be handled as out-of-band rollouts; we will notify 4h in advance when possible. (Matches Rachel).
- Canary sizing: recommend two parallel canaries on separate racks to exercise KV cache warm-up; expect 2–8% CPU delta during initial tokenization passes. Canary duration: 48 hours with automated health checks (latency P95, error rate, KV miss rate).
- Fast-unpin mechanics: the control plane will flip routing rules and invalidate prefixes; full KV eviction and cold-starts may take up to 90 minutes for large-state models — we add an advisory to customers.
- Communications: preflight doc shared 24h before, live bridge during rollout, and a postmortem in 72h if any rollback occurs.

James/Sasha: do you have preferred SLAs for notification and any internal blackout dates in November/December? Also confirm whether your on-prem connector is behind a NAT that blocks out-bound gRPC on ephemeral ports — that changes canary behavior.

-Karthik
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

James / Sasha — following up to confirm an operational plan based on your checklist and the notes below. We propose the following concrete schedule this month for alignment and an initial validation run:

- Wed, Nov 24 02:00–04:00 PT — Staging canary: 2-node canary in your staging VPC; we will run the GA->patched variant and collect the 48h health window. (Action: Orion to approve access; Redwood to start canary)
- Mon, Nov 30 02:00–03:30 PT — Dry-run: orchestration rehearsal with simulated rollback and communication bridge. (Action: both teams on bridge)
- Dec 7–9 — Production maintenance window (single short maintenance window per region); final dates locked after staging success.

Rollback acceptance criteria (short):
- Latency P95 regression < 30% and error-rate delta < 0.5% within canary window
- No KV miss spike > 12% sustained beyond 10 minutes
- System health checks (ingress queue, worker liveness) green for 30m post-rollout

Deliverables we will share before the canary:
- Read-only runbook (shared Drive link) — runbook includes exact CLI commands for pin/unpin, expected logs, and audit entries.
- Preflight checklist mapped to OrionBank_Security-Checklist.pdf (we reference section numbers).
- Live bridge dial-in and escalation contact list.

If this matches your needs we’ll send a DocuSign PO amendment and kickoff the staging access workstream.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Rachel
